title: Strassen’s asymptotic rank conjecture
formal: For every \(n\ge 1\) and every tensor \(T\in \mathbb{C} ^{n}\otimes \mathbb{C} ^{n}\otimes \mathbb{C} ^{n}\) whose three flattenings all have rank n, is \(\lim _{k\to \infty} R(T^{\otimes}k)^{1/k}=n\)?
definitions: \(R(T)\) is the least r such that \(T=\sum_{i=1}^{r} a_{i}\otimes b_{i}\otimes c_{i}\) with \(a_{i},b_{i},c_{i}\in \mathbb{C} ^{n}\). Each flattening views the tensor as a linear map from the dual of one factor into the tensor product of the other two. In \(T^{\otimes}k\) the first, second and third tensor factors are respectively grouped, producing a tensor with three factors \(\mathbb{C} ^{n^{k}}\). Submultiplicativity of rank makes the displayed limit equal to \(\inf _{k\ge 1} R(T^{\otimes}k)^{1/k}\). This is exact rank over \(\mathbb{C}\), not border rank, and there is no explicitness or computational requirement on T.

context_blocks.text: Matrix rank has a simple algebraic characterization, whereas tensor rank changes substantially when many independent copies are considered jointly. Strassen’s conjecture says that in the asymptotic setting the three flattening dimensions already determine the answer.

The cubic concise formulation is the target proposed in the personal list. It includes matrix-multiplication tensors, so a positive resolution would imply matrix multiplication exponent two; the reverse implication is not claimed. The 2024–2026 source studies structural properties of asymptotic rank without proving this equality.

why: A structural conjecture about the cost of all bilinear computations, extending well beyond one matrix-multiplication algorithm.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
